content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"This judge text resolves a pressed link by treating Matthew 1:16 as underdetermined from its own grammar, so it is doing the verse-by-verse weighing that K-C governs.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D1 vs C2 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē (was born) with feminine hēs (of whom) admits both the withheld-father and the birth-narration readings","rule_words":"When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.","room":"weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse — one reading forbids the judge from resolving a pressed link by finding one verse ambiguous in itself; the other permits noting a single verse is underdetermined while leaving the chain to be weighed by footing.","why":"The judge marks Matthew 1:16 UNDERDETERMINED because its grammar admits two readings, which is a verse-level test rather than the chain-against-chain footing K-C requires."}
